intro: Two ways to do it: gut it whole, or the gutless method (quarter it where it lies and never open the belly). Gutless is lighter to pack out and keeps the meat cleaner. Either way, cool the meat fast: get the hide off, the meat in game bags, and air moving around it.

law.title: Colorado: evidence of sex
rules: Sign and detach your carcass tag right after the kill, and fasten it to the carcass (not the head or hide).
Evidence of sex must stay naturally attached. A head cut off the carcass doesn't count.
Bull: the head with antlers, or a testicle, the scrotum or the penis, still attached.
Cow: the head, the udder or the vulva, still attached.
Cut in pieces or boned out: the evidence has to stay attached to a quarter or another major piece, and every piece travels together.
Antler point units: leave the head (or skull plate) with both antlers attached to a piece of the carcass to prove the bull is legal.
You must pack out at least the four quarters, both backstraps and both tenderloins. Leaving meat to waste is illegal.
If you send the head in for CWD testing, keep the evidence of sex on the carcass.
law.note: Rules change; check this year's CPW Big Game brochure before you hunt.

bull.label: Bull
bull.evidence: Keep one testicle in its scrotum attached to a hindquarter.
how: Before any other cut, find the scrotum between the hind legs.
Cut the hide in a loop well out around it, so a patch of hide stays with the testicle.
Leave that patch connected to the hide of one hindquarter. Skin that quarter around it, not through it, so the testicle rides on that quarter all the way home.
Cut the penis free along the belly back to the pelvis. You don't need it once a testicle is kept.
Antler point unit? The head or the skull plate with both antlers stays with the carcass too.

cow.label: Cow
cow.evidence: Keep the udder (or the vulva) attached to a hindquarter.
how: Before any other cut, find the udder between the hind legs.
Run the belly cut beside the udder, not through it.
Skin the udder off the belly toward one hind leg, but leave it attached to that hindquarter's hide.
Skin that quarter around the udder so it stays on the quarter all the way home.
Milk in the udder sours meat: keep the udder's cut side off the meat, and trim any meat it soaks.

methods.name: Gutless (quarter it in place)
methods.summary: Best for elk you pack out on your back. The body cavity is never opened, so the bladder and rectum never come into it.

steps.t: Tag it and take your photos.
steps.d: Sign and detach the carcass tag and fasten it on. Lay out game bags, knife, spare blades, saw (if keeping the skull plate) and paracord.

steps.t: Mark the evidence of sex first.
steps.d: Find it before you cut anything else. Pick the quarter it rides on (the down-side hindquarter is easiest) and skin around it, never through it. See the Colorado box above.

steps.t: Lay it on its side, back uphill.
steps.d: Cut the hide down the spine from the neck to the tail, then down the back of each leg. Skin the top side down to the belly and lay the hide out flat as a clean tarp for the meat.
Lift the leg and cut flat along the ribs under it. There is no ball joint, just meat; it comes free. Bag it.

Cut along the pelvis to the ball joint. Pull the leg out to pop the joint, cut around the ball, and take it off. Keep the tip clear of the belly. If the evidence of sex is on this quarter, check it is still attached. Bag it.
Cut along the spine from the hip to the neck, then along the top of the ribs, and peel it out in one long piece.
Take the neck meat off both sides, and strip the meat between and over the ribs for grind.

Push the belly meat down behind the last rib and cut a hand-sized window through the thin wall in front of the hip. Reach in along the spine and work the tenderloin free with your fingers, cutting each end. Everything else stays in its sack.
Flip the carcass onto the clean hide side and do the other half the same way.
Hang the bags in shade with air around them; don't pile them. Get them below 40 °F as soon as you can.

methods.name: Gut it whole
methods.summary: When you can drag or drive to it. Clear the pelvis without splitting it, and keep the paunch and bladder whole.

steps.t: Tag it and take your photos.
steps.d: Sign and detach the carcass tag and fasten it on. Gloves on.
Prop it with rocks or tie the legs out. Gravity pulls the guts back out of your way.
Route every cut around it, never through it, so it stays attached toward one hind leg. See the Colorado box above.

Cut a deep circle around the anus (and the vulva on a cow, unless it's your evidence of sex), 3–4 inches in, angled toward the spine, staying close to the pelvic bone. Pull it out a few inches and tie it off tight with string or a zip tie. Then push it back inside the pelvis.

Pinch up the skin at the bottom of the belly and nick it. Slide two fingers in, palm up, with the blade between them, edge up, and lift as you cut forward to the breastbone. You're cutting hide and the thin muscle only; never the paunch.
Cut the sheet of muscle that separates the chest from the belly, around the inside of the ribs.
Reach up into the chest as far toward the throat as you can, grab the windpipe and gullet together and cut them above your hand.
Pull the windpipe back and down, and the heart, lungs and stomach come with it. Free the tissue holding them along the spine as you go.

steps.t: Bring the bladder and rectum out through the pelvis.
steps.d: Reach in, find the tied-off rectum and the bladder, and draw them forward and out through the pelvic opening from the inside. No splitting the pelvis.
Wipe out blood and anything spilled with a dry cloth or snow. Prop the cavity open with a stick, get the hide off as soon as you can, and get the quarters into game bags in the shade.

rectum.title: The rear end, without splitting the pelvis
items: Core it, don't split it. A deep circle around the anus with a short, stiff blade, cut toward the spine and kept tight to the bone, frees it so it pulls through the pelvic opening from inside.
Tie it off before it moves. String, a zip tie or a rubber band, right behind where you cut. Or slip a sandwich bag over the end first and tie it over the bag.
Push the tied end back in, so it comes out the front with the guts instead of being dragged across the hams.
If something spills, trim it away. Don't wipe it around, and don't wash it in unless you can dry the meat after.
Gutless method: you don't touch the rear end at all.

bladder.title: The bladder, without spilling it
items: Find it by feel: a soft balloon in the pelvis, on the belly side of the rectum. It may be full.
Pinch its neck shut with your fingers (or tie it off) and keep it pinched while you cut beyond your fingers.
Lift it straight out, away from the meat, and set it downhill.
If it leaks onto meat: rinse with clean water right away, dry it, and trim the soaked meat. Urine taints meat fast.
On a bull, follow the penis back to it: free the penis along the belly first and it leads you to the bladder neck.

paunch.title: Not cutting into the gut
items: Two fingers under the blade, edge up, on the belly cut. The paunch lies right under the wall.
Short blade or a gut hook for that cut.
If the paunch is nicked, keep cutting slow, finish, roll the guts out, and wipe the cavity clean and dry.
